Those returns dwarf Nordic peers such as Skanska (~12%) and NCC (~10%). # Veidekke ASA (VEI.OL) — A Deep Dive on Management and the Setup

*Prepared for the investment committee. No earnings-call transcript was bundled with this name; the analysis below draws on Veidekke's published Q4 2025 / full-year 2025 results (released February 12, 2026), the Q1 2026 report (released May 7, 2026), the company's spring 2026 market update, and its stated 2030 targets, all retrieved from the web and dated where it matters.*

Veidekke is one of Scandinavia's largest construction and civil-engineering groups, based in Norway with sizeable operations in Sweden. It builds homes and commercial buildings (its "Construction" / Bygg arm), builds roads, rail and other heavy infrastructure (its "Infrastructure" / Anlegg arm, split Norway and Sweden), and runs an asphalt and aggregates industrial business. It is run as a low-capital, project-execution business: it carries almost no net debt, pays out most of its earnings as dividends, and earns unusually high returns on the small amount of capital it does employ.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story Veidekke has told over the past two years is a steady, unflashy one: *fix the margin, hold the discipline, let the cycle come back.* After the 2022–2023 cost-inflation shock that squeezed every Nordic contractor, management's central message has been operational improvement rather than expansion — better project selection, better capacity utilisation, and tighter risk control on fixed-price work. That message has held remarkably constant.

The most recent inflection is genuinely positive. Coming out of full-year 2025 (reported February 2026), management shifted from "we are repairing profitability" to "the market is turning." The company now guides to roughly 5% activity growth in 2026 and 4% in 2027, with the recovery led by residential and small-housing construction — the very segment that was hit hardest in the downturn. By the Q1 2026 report (May 2026), that confidence was backed by hard order intake: the 12-month order backlog was up 8% year over year, with a "particularly strong book-to-bill in Bygg [Construction]," and asphalt season bookings rose to roughly 775,000 tonnes on national and county road contracts (from 640,000 a year earlier).

What has *not* changed — and this is the crux for a value committee — is the valuation framing. Nothing in the narrative arc suggests a hidden, mispriced asset or a coming corporate event. This is an operationally improving cyclical at the upswing of its cycle, telling a clean and credible story that the market already hears.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

The screener metrics on this name are partly corrupted and must be read with care before testing any claim against them.

| Management / screener claim | The actual financials | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "We improved profitability across all business areas in 2025" | Pre-tax profit NOK 2,057M in 2025, up 22% from NOK 1,683M; EBT margin 4.8% vs 4.1% in 2024; net income NOK 1.55B vs 1.26B; EPS 11.5 vs 9.3 (+23.7%) | **Holds.** The margin repair is real and broad-based, corroborated by the multi-year trajectory (net income up every year 2023→2025). |
| Screener: "Gross margin 100.0% (expanding)" | A data artifact. Contractors book revenue net of subcontractors; the feed mislabels this as a 100% gross margin. | **Does not hold up — discard.** The peer file flags the same artifact. Use net margin (~3.6%) and EBT margin (4.8%), which are normal-to-good for construction. |
| Screener: "Fair Value 14.0, Margin of Safety −99%, P/FCF 96x" | Downstream of the same artifact and a single trailing-FCF quirk. On real earnings (EPS ~11.5–11.7) at ~NOK 180, the price-to-earnings ratio is ~15.6x — a normal multiple, not 96x. | **Does not hold up — discard.** Every per-method margin-of-safety reads −100%, which is the model failing on bad inputs, not a genuine 99% overvaluation. |
| "Capital-efficient growth; strong balance sheet" | Net interest-bearing *position* of about NOK 4.6B (net cash) at Q1 2026, up from NOK 2.7B a year earlier; Q1 operating cash flow ~NOK 900M; the live correction in our inputs recomputes net cash at about NOK 4.36B. ROE 37.2%, ROIC 20.0%. | **Holds, and is the single best fact here.** This is a debt-free, cash-generative, high-return contractor — genuinely higher quality than most Nordic peers (Skanska ROIC ~12%, NCC ~10%). |
| "Order backlog supports the growth outlook" | 12-month backlog +8% YoY at Q1 2026; consistent 6–8% activity-growth trend | **Holds.** Forward visibility is improving, consistent with the 2026/2027 guide. |

The honest read: where the *narrative* is testable against clean numbers (margin repair, balance-sheet strength, order growth, returns on capital), it holds up well. Where the *screener* makes this look like a screaming value name (96x price-to-free-cash-flow, −99% margin of safety, a NOK 14 fair value against a NOK 191 price), the screener is simply wrong — these are artifacts, not a thesis.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rising.** With no transcript bundled, this is inferred from the published reports and guidance, but the direction is unambiguous. Through 2024 the language was defensive and repair-oriented (capacity, discipline, project selection). By the February 2026 full-year report the company explicitly called a cyclical turn ("moderate upturn from 2026") and put numbers on it (5% growth in 2026, 4% in 2027). The Q1 2026 report then validated the optimism with a strong book-to-bill rather than walking it back. The shift is from defensive to cautiously offensive — but "cautiously" is the operative word; this is not a management team promising a step-change.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Medium-to-High.** The financials show earnings beats in 5 of the last 7 quarters (about 71%), and the multi-year delivery is clean: profit and margin both rose in 2024 and again in 2025, exactly as the "improvement programme" promised. The 2030 framework — long-term pre-tax margin above 5%, revenue growth ~2.5 points above the market, and a dividend policy of distributing more than 70% of earnings per share — is specific and conservative rather than promotional. Management tends to set achievable targets and hit them. The main credibility caveat is structural, not behavioural: construction earnings are cyclical and fixed-price project risk can turn a good year into a write-down year, so even an honest team's guidance carries cycle risk.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

The recurring tension is valuation, not operations. The street's own consensus recommendation on the stock is "sell," with an average twelve-month price target (around NOK 184–188) barely above the current price (~NOK 180) — analysts like the company and dislike the price. The pressure point a buyer must answer is simple: at ~15.6x earnings and roughly 86% of the way up its 52-week range, sitting above its 200-day average, what is left to capture in a contractor whose own guidance is "moderate" growth? There is no segment the market is ignoring and no asset it is missing.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🟢 Margin repair delivered and broad-based (EBT margin 4.8%, +22% pre-tax profit in 2025).
🟢 Fortress balance sheet: ~NOK 4.4–4.6B net cash, essentially no debt, Altman-Z solvency 3.8.
🟢 Best-in-class returns for the peer set: ROIC ~20%, ROE ~37%.
🟢 Order backlog +8% and a cyclical recovery the company can now point to in its own bookings.

🔴 Valuation, full stop. The stock is rich versus its Scandinavian construction peers (AF Gruppen typically 8–12x free cash flow; Veidekke screens far above on any cash-flow multiple), and it sits near a 52-week high with the street rating it "sell."
🔴 The only discrete catalyst — the NOK 11.25 per-share dividend — has already been paid (ex-dividend May 7, 2026; paid May 20, 2026). The income event the yield-focused base was waiting for is behind us, not ahead.
🔴 Cyclical and fixed-price risk: a Nordic construction recovery is real but fragile, rate-sensitive (the Norwegian and Swedish rate path matters), and one large troubled project can dent a year.
🔴 The "deep value" label on this candidate is an artifact. Every genuine valuation method on clean inputs says fairly-to-richly valued, not cheap.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The most important "hidden" signal is what the corrected inputs reveal: the screener's deep-value flag is built on a broken gross-margin field and a single trailing-FCF distortion, and the only model that fired (enterprise value to gross profit) is, as the peer note says, "a loose signal" on a margin-compressed contractor. Strip those away and there is no concealed cheapness. The genuinely under-appreciated fact is the *quality* of the balance sheet and returns — but quality is not the same as a mispricing, and the market is already paying a peer-premium multiple precisely because it sees that quality.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE** — arguably strengthening operationally, but stable as an investment proposition. Veidekke is a well-run, debt-free, high-return Nordic contractor at the early-to-mid stage of a cyclical recovery, trading at a full peer-premium multiple near its 52-week high, with its one discrete catalyst (the dividend) already paid.

The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: **this is not a deep-value special situation; it is a quality cyclical at a fair-to-rich price with no live catalyst.** Any position is a bet on the Nordic construction cycle continuing and the premium multiple holding — not on a discount closing. There is no margin of safety to lean on if the cycle stalls or a project goes wrong.

On the economic moat: Veidekke's advantage is a **scale-cost and local-execution edge** (regional density in asphalt and infrastructure, brand and relationships in a relationship-driven bid market) — real but **narrow**, the normal moat of a strong contractor, not a wide structural fortress. Construction is a low-margin, competitively-bid, commoditised-service industry; the company's high returns come from running it unusually well and keeping capital light, not from pricing power. The moat is **stable** (returns are high and steady, not eroding). There is **no terminal secular threat**: construction demand is cyclical, not structurally shrinking, and no technology or channel shift is collapsing this business's terminal value — the risk here is cyclical and valuation, not a melting base. No secular-decline theme applies.
